{"notes": "VISIT 3 (left 5:15). Table: body, lower fork (to ~26,14.7) and most of the upper lobe are dark and connected. The upper lobe tip, about 4 dominoes near (27-29, 7.5-8), is pale and disconnected, so that is the main open gap. The belly is a dense double line near (13-16, 14) but connected. I still can't tell who placed what, so I'm not crediting anyone for the build itself.

TOM: Accepted Priya's ownership of the lower fork cleanly and said he'd finish the body end, then check tail joins. Good collaboration again (3 observations) and leadership is plausible. I haven't yet seen him find or fix a gap, and he isn't visibly on the pale tip. Check next visit.

PRIYA: Now clearly active. She replied to Tom, claimed the lower fork, split the work and asked for a join check. That is clear, accurate communication, and the lower fork is dark and complete, matching her claim. Collaboration is positive. Earlier silence is resolved, so don't penalise it.

MAYA: Tracks the upper lobe and the bin supply. But she misheard Priya's handover, telling Tom the fork was his, and called the lobe 'done' while its tip is still pale. She did notice the pale dominoes and went to check joins. Mixed on execution. Ask her privately what she placed.

LEO: First contribution was at 5:00. He offered to close a lower-fork gap, but I see no gap there. He flagged a break in the upper lobe, which is real (the pale tip), though he placed it near the top of the curve. Useful eye, but his claim is unverified. Ask him privately.

OPEN: Does anyone close the upper tip before time? Does the fish fall as one piece? No ratings yet."}
